title: Tom Jackson, former Broncos star and Hall of Fame broadcaster at ESPN, dies at 75 | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Tom Jackson, a former NFL linebacker and Hall of Fame broadcaster, has died at the age of 75.

His longtime employer ESPN announced his death on Sunday, after his family informed the network on Friday.

Jackson was a fourth-round pick by the Broncos in the 1973 draft out of Louisville; Jackson played in 191 regular-season games, including 177 starts as a member of Denver’s “Orange Crush” defense. He was a three-time Pro Bowl selection and a two-time AP All-Pro.

After his retirement from football in 1986, he joined ESPN where he spent 29 years and was most well-known for his role alongside Chris Berman.

Berman said Jackson’s death was “unexpected” on Sunday and added that he spoke to him “at length” last week after he made a surprise appearance at the studio.

“He was a vital 75,” an emotional Berman said on ESPN’s “Sunday NFL Countdown.”

“Tom was poignant. He was active. This is a shock.”

In a statement released by ESPN, Berman said that Jackson was “one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet.”

“All of us are stunned,” Berman said in hisstatement. “I’m stunned, we’re stunned and you’re stunned. We’ve lost one of the best human beings ever to walk the planet, Tom Jackson. I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown. It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.”

ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro called Jackson “one of the most influential and beloved figures in ESPN’s history.”

“He brought the credibility of an All-Pro NFL player, the insight of a gifted analyst and a warmth and authenticity that connected with generations of football fans,” Pitaro said in astatement. “Alongside Chris Berman, he helped make NFL Primetime an iconic part of our football weekends. In fact, ESPN’s NFL studio is named the Chris Berman-Tom Jackson Studio, a distinction unmatched in our history and a fitting tribute to their lasting impact.

“Away from the set, Tom was a trusted colleague, generous mentor and dear friend to many. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends, former teammates and all who loved him. His legacy at ESPN, throughout the NFL and among the countless fans who admired his incredible work will endure.”

Jackson was awarded the Pete Rozelle Radio-Television award by the Hall of Fame in 2015 and retired from ESPN a year later after covering the Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinement ceremony.

“Tom was so much more than an accomplished NFL analyst,” Berman continued in his statement. “There was nobody kinder, more thoughtful, more loyal or more engaging than him. And when it came to laughter, Tom’s was frequent and unmistakable. He is easily summed up by this classic old song: ‘He’s got sunshine on a cloudy day.’”

Jackson is survived by his wife Jen and his daughters Taylor and Morgan.

“Our hearts bleed for them. We thank them for lending Tom to us. Tom was my best friend professionally and personally. If you ever met him or just knew him from watching ESPN, he was your best friend too,” Berman said.

This story has been updated with additional information.
